Mr. Khondker Mahbubuddin Ahmed with Mr. Abdul Malek and Mr. Raquibul Haque Miah, Advocates for the Petitioner
Mr. A.F. Masan Ariff, D.A.G. with Mr Amirul Kabir Chowdhury, and Mr. Syed Abu Kawsar, A.A.G., for the State
parties:
Khondker Maniruzzaman ------ Petitioner
Vs.
The State ----- Opposite Party
full_judgment:
Mahfuzur Rahman, J: This Rule was issued on an application under section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure upon the opposite party at the instance of the accused petitioner to show cause as to why the order dated 19.6.94 framing charge against the petitioner under sections 302/109 and 307/109 of the Penal Code in Sessions Case No. 120 of 1993 by Additional Sessions Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka should not be set aside. 

 2. The short fact relevant for the purpose of disposal of the Rule in brief is that the petitioner Khondker Moniruzzaman a General Manager (Vigilence) of Titas Gas Transmission and Distribution Co. Ltd. lodged an ejhar with the Tejgaon Police Station on 9.7.92 alleging that on the same date i.e. on 9.7.92 at 8/9 A.M. the members and supporters of the rival Unions of the employees of the Titas Gas Transmission and Distribution Company Limited assembled in the Executive floor of the Titas Gas Building at Kawran Bazar. At this to avoid any untoward event the Security Inspector of the said Company Mr. M.A. Basher informed the police over telephone about the situation and sought for help at 8.15 A.M. and again at 8.30 A.M. when the situation further detoriated but with no response. All on a sudden at about 9.45 A.M. the members of the rival groups of the Unions became violent and started assaulting each other and inconsequence thereof the office rooms were ransacked, the doors, windows together with the furniture’s etc. were broken and damaged causing a loss of more than Tk. 4.50 Lacs. During the occurrence one Bellal Hossain a Supervisor of the Titas Gas and a Trade Union Worker belonging to the rival group of the accused persons jumped from the 4/5th floor of the building on the ground out of fear or was thrown away by some of the miscreants. As a result of which he received multiple injuries and was taken to Hospital where he died. On the previous day of occurrence i.e. 8.7.92 the Members of the Unions No. 1880 and 1939 held meeting at the gate of the office at 7-45 hours and in a procession entered into the Executive Floor of the Titas Gas Building and at that time the members of Union No. 1940 entered into that floor and started fighting and the situation ultimately was controlled at the intervention of the police. Thereafter the representatives of the rival groups submitted memorandum to the Managing Director and left the Executive Floor. 

 3. On receiving the F.I.R. lodged by the petitioner Mr. Khondker Moniruzzaman, police started Tejgaon P.S. Case No. 22(7)92 under sections 147/148/149/323/324/325/327/307/302 of the Penal Code and took up investigation of the same. 

 6. Thereafter the case record was transmit-ted to the Court of the learned Sessions Judge, Dhaka which was registered as Sessions Case No. 120 of 1993 and the learned Sessions Judge then transferred the same to the Court of Additional Sessions Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka for trial. The learned Additional Sessions Judge on receiving the case record fixed 30.9.93 for framing charge against the accused persons. The accused petitioner Khondker Moniruzzaman filed an application under section 265C of the Code of Criminal Procedure praying for discharging him from the case contending that he has been falsely implicated in the case with ulterior motive and that there is no material on record to implicate him in the occurrence and that on his information the case has been started. The other accused persons also filed similar applications. The learned Additional Sessions Judge after hearing by his order dated 30.9.93 framed charge against all other accused persons under different sections of the Penal Code and the petitioner was charged only under section 201 of the Penal Code. 

 8. On receiving the case record from this Court the learned Additional Sessions Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka after hearing framed charge against the accused petitioner under sections 302/109 and 307/109 of the Penal Code by her order dated 19.6.94. 

 10. Mr. Khandker Mahbubuddin Ahmed the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the learned Additional Sessions Judge committed an error of law in framing charge against the accused petitioner under sections 302/109 and 307/109 of the Penal Code on total misreading of the provision of section 107 of the Penal Code. He submits that from the findings of the learned Additional Sessions Judge and from the recorded facts it is abundantly clear that at any point of time, when the occurrence was going on or alleged bringing out arms, lathie etc. from the office room of the petitioner, he was not at all present there. It is also not in the 161 Cr.P.C. statements of the witnesses that the petitioner was in any way connected with the occurrence and did any act of abetment. lie next contends that even in the F.I.R. lodged on the following day by one S.M. Zillur Rahman, which was treated as G.D. Entry by the police, the names of 22 accused were mentioned, but the name of the petitioner was neither mentioned, nor any allegation was made to the effect that other accused brought out weapons from the room of the present petitioner. No act of abetment has been alleged against the petitioner and nothing has been stated therein that the petitioner was ever seen at the place of occurrence or present in his office room at the relevant time. He submits that the learned Additional Sessions Judge on misconception of law and misreading of the facts of the case framed charge of abetment against the petitioner which cannot be sustained in law. Mr. Ahmed next submits since on the recorded facts there is no iota of evidence of any act of abetment, the learned Additional Sessions Judge committed an illegality in framing charge against the petitioner under sections 302/109 and 307/109 of the Penal Code which is liable to be set aside. 

 "265C. If, upon consideration of the record of the case and the documents submitted therewith, and after hearing the submissions of the accused and the prosecution in this behalf, the Court considers that there is no sufficient ground for proceeding against the accused, it shall discharge the accused and record the reasons for so doing." 

 14. Now the law is settled by our judicial pronouncement of this Court that this Court under section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure having supervisory jurisdiction can scrutinize and go into facts to examine the propriety of the impugned order passed under section 265C or 265D of the Code. In the case of A.K.M. Mohinus Saleh and others Vs. State, reported in 45 D.L.R. (H.C.D) page 386 it has been held that: 

 15. In the result, the Rule is made absolute. The judgment and order passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka on 19.6.94 in Sessions Case No. 120 of 1993 framing charge against the accused petitioner under sections 302/109 and 307/109 of the Penal Code is hereby set aside and the petitioner Khondker Moniruzaman is discharged from the Sessions Case No. 120 of 1993 arising out of Tejgaon P.S. Case No. 22(7) 92 being G.R. Case No. 3048/92 under section 265C of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
